title: release-notes-ontology-and-automated-signoff-bot-integration
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Create a structured release-notes ontology and a lightweight signoff automation (Slack+GitHub) to accelerate drafting, ensure cross-team approvals, and support redaction/policy checks for both internal and customer-facing changelogs. Deliverables: 1) JSON-LD schema for release items (type, risk, migration, visibility, owners, links), 2) Confluence + Drive templates that render from schema, 3) Signoff bot that posts draft summaries, collects approvals and adds a GitHub check linked to the final release note, 4) Redaction rules and PII check integration with security team.
acceptance_criteria: Schema defined in JSON-LD and checked into docs repo (schema file + example payload)
Automated bot posts generated draft to #release-review Slack channel with thread-based approvals and records approvals as GitHub check
PM/Eng/Design approvers list is configurable via a simple YAML file in the repo
Customer-facing notes auto-render from schema and pass the security redaction checklist (no PII/credentials)
Integration tests: signoff flow exercised in staging with at least two mock releases and documented runbook
tasks: Draft JSON-LD ontology and example mapping for common change types (feature, bugfix, breaking-change, deprecated, security)
Convene 1-hour alignment session with Eng/Design/Security to validate fields and visibility rules (agenda + notes)
Prototype signoff bot (Slack app + GitHub Action) that creates a draft PR containing release-notes.json and a human-readable markdown render
Add redaction check step that runs a regex-based PII scan and queries KMS audit flags before marking as approved
Create Confluence template + Drive auto-export (PDF/HTML) from schema for Customer Success and Sales to consume
Smoke tests and CI jobs: unit tests for schema validation and E2E for signoff flow
comments: 2025-02-28 - Aisha Kumar: Initial ticket created. Goal is to reduce manual back-and-forth and make release notes machine-readable so downstream systems (release emails, Status page, SDK changelogs) can consume the canonical source.

2025-03-03 - Liam Ortega: POC signoff bot deployed to staging. It posts drafts to #release-review and creates a draft PR. Still working on mapping approvals to GitHub checks. Pushed prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/214

2025-03-04 - Priya Shah (Security): Reviewed redaction rules. Requested addition: block any snippet with 20+ contiguous alphanumeric characters (likely tokens/keys) and require manual override flag. See notes: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/Sec/pages/AI-Redaction-Checklist

2025-03-05 - Marco Diaz (Design): Reviewed customer-facing render. Suggested adding a short 'What changed for developers' line to all customer entries and collapsing internal-only technical details behind an 'advanced details' toggle in the rendered view.

2025-03-06 - Liam Ortega: Marking 'schema stable' after incorporating Security's override flag and Design's summary line. Requesting final PM + Eng approval before we flip the bot to production. Updated draft template: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cSample
decision_log: 2025-03-03: Adopt JSON-LD as canonical format to allow typed fields and easy expansion by integrations.
2025-03-04: Require explicit 'visibility' field (internal|public|partner) and enforce via signoff bot checks.
2025-03-05: Security requested override flag for redaction failures; agreed to add 'manual_redaction_required' boolean and a documented waiver process.
2025-03-06: Use GitHub Checks API to record final approval state; bot will create a check-run referencing the draft PR and list approvers in the check summary.
audit_trail: 2025-03-03: Status moved to In Progress (owner: Liam Ortega)
2025-03-06: Status moved to In Review; schema marked stable
notes: Next steps: 1) Final signoff from Eng (Evan) and CS (Sophie) by 2025-03-10, 2) Run two staged releases via staging environment, 3) Add docs page for release authors with examples and a small CLI helper to generate schema payloads from a markdown template. If approvals are received, plan production roll flip on 2025-03-12.
